title: Knowledge check: Typed Reactivity and Composition API

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Typed Reactivity and Composition API”?
options: Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
Type annotations automatically validate HTTP response objects at runtime.
Every Vue 3 application must use TypeScript.
A type checker replaces browser and component tests.
questions.answer_key: Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Typed Reactivity and Composition API directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Typing refs and reactive objects”, which practice is most reliable?
options: reactive() turns every primitive into a ref automatically.
Destructuring always preserves a reactive link to each primitive property.
A reactive object must be copied into local state before every update.
Use reactive() for an object whose nested properties are tracked, and avoid destructuring in ways that lose the property connection.
questions.answer_key: Use reactive() for an object whose nested properties are tracked, and avoid destructuring in ways that lose the property connection.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Typing refs and reactive objects”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Typed Reactivity and Composition API” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
